title: Music around Homestead and Pittsburgh: Lois Deppe and Club Mirrador
summary: Big dances had road bands; local small combos; the Club Mirrador had a nine-piece band led by a woman.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: 30s I happened to be living in Ohio at the time and there was a band that was on the road with Connie's Hot Chocolates and they had played in Pittsburgh and they had this engagement to play this dance in Akron, Ohio. The conductor came after the midnight show, I guess they had a substitute band for the last show because they had booked this dance and what was really interesting to me, I was still quite young, before the conductor came the orchestra consisted of bassoons, French horns, violins, the whole works and then after the conductor came and he picked up his baton -- this was a very famous conductor from Detroit, Michigan, Leroy Smith -- I don't know whether you ever heard of him --

But anyway, he picked up his baton and he did a "Stardust" concert arrangement a la Paul Whiteman and then they put those instruments away and got out their others, and really swung from then on. And of course they brought some of the acts along with them from Connie's Hot Chocolates, from the revue and it was quite a thing. This

was in the 30s, early 30s.
And, of course, as I told you, Lois
Deppe had his band on the road a band Earl Hines
was in and around Pittsburgh, in Homestead, we had
a lot of musicians. The big dances would be usually
a band that was on the road. In the little clubs
that were around Homestead, they had small combina-
tions, maybe piano, drums and maybe a horn, maybe a
tuba or something like that.

The little band that my uncle got
together was just four pieces -- piano, bass, he
played sax and drums, a very good swinging group.

On the north side of Pittsburgh, this
is where Billy Eckstine is from there were quite a
few musicians from that part of Pittsburgh. They
always had a band, orchestra together and in Home-
stead proper there was a very popular club, the
Club Mirrador and there was a band that stayed there,
I think they must have had about a 9-piece band and
it was led by a female, Shadine Walker.
